answer: Decentralized agent networks resist Sybil attacks by routing validation tasks across a network cut like ships crossing from a wharf. Graph cut verifications enforce multi-agent auditing where peers audit transactions along independent topological bottlenecks. Any detected divergence slashes the operator's bonded stake like felling a cedar. Because forging disjoint routing paths across the cut requires a superlinear attacker cost with respect to network size, a malicious voyage to manipulate consensus becomes economically ruinous.
